identity: Joe Brainard’s named book-length work, with explicit author disambiguation, distinct from anaphora itself and from exercises modeled on it.
qualifications: Ordinary recollections and accumulation are supported by the described form and quoted examples. The teaching influence is expressly documented.
claims: Recurring initial words organize separate memories into a book
Lines 48–51 identify book-length repetition and everyday recollections.
The device became a writing-exercise model
Line 52 explicitly credits Koch’s adaptation and later instructional popularity.
relations: The Academy expressly identifies I Remember as an example of anaphora; the pinned target is rhetorical initial-word recurrence, not another anaphora sense.

identity: Data-dependent cluster/gap classification, distinct from quantile equal counts and equal-interval fixed widths. Facet/application scope reflects a specific mapping decision.
qualifications: Can reveal and may hinder avoid guarantees; datasets classified separately retain the source’s comparability warning.
claims: Natural breaks groups similar values and places breaks near gaps
Paragraph 9 explicitly explains the grouping rule.
Dataset-specific thresholds limit comparison across separately classified maps
Paragraph 10 directly states this drawback.
relations: The source explicitly organizes natural breaks and quantile as alternative mapping classifications with contrasting rules, supporting the comparison without asserting a hierarchy.
Cartography broader-topic connection is clearly editorial and grounded in map symbolization plus the pinned field meaning.

identity: Existing registered Shinto broad-field control; the ofuda example does not create a new identity or reduce the whole tradition to that object.
qualifications: Shrine traditions identifies the covered setting; sacred objects are treated with reverence rather than their powers presented as experimentally established.
claims: Jinja enshrine and venerate kami, with visits and festivals
Opening 6–9 explicitly connects jinja, Shinto, kami and matsuri.
An ofuda extends shrine practice into the household
r08 paragraph 15 gives household altar placement, while r21 line 46 links received shrine objects and protection.
relations: Both sources explicitly connect ofuda with receiving kami-related sacred objects at Shinto shrines and keeping them close or at home. The actual link is supported.

identity: Existing Color theory topic control; examples of contrast remain facets of the general color-interaction meaning.
qualifications: Appearance depends partly on context; it does not say pigments themselves change or these are the only determinants.
claims: Color appearance varies with neighboring colors
Glossary 316 explicitly distinguishes altered perception from unchanged colors.
Previously viewed colors can affect subsequent appearance
Glossary 317 describes successive contrast and retained afterimage.
relations: The same lesson explicitly teaches color theory at line 228 and defines simultaneous contrast at 316, supporting the field-to-example relationship.

identity: Existing Archaeology broad-field control. Context is a separately learnable method, not a second identity for the entire field.
qualifications: Reconstruction is grounded in material context; does not imply every artifact supplies a definitive complete story.
claims: Archaeology studies past lives through objects, features and environmental remains
The archaeologist definition and artifact/ecofact/feature list support each category.
Location and associations give finds historical interpretability
Context paragraphs 23–30 document associations and explain the need to record them.
relations: Editorial related_to correctly uses context as an explanatory entry point into archaeology. The factual relation is also explicit in the NPS discussion; no false prerequisite/equivalence is claimed.

identity: Elizabeth Bishop’s specific poem, distinct from the villanelle form and from other poems about loss. Named-subject idea scope is appropriate.
qualifications: The discovery card explicitly labels its reading editorial. Increasing emotional difficulty is a defensible reading of the changing refrain, not a biographical diagnosis. If takeaway is ever displayed alone, preserve this interpretive cue there too.
claims: The poem moves from everyday misplacements toward intimate loss
Read the full poem at 38–60; early everyday objects and final address establish that progression.
The returning lines can sound increasingly strained
Variation near the end and the speaker’s closing self-command support the explicitly marked editorial reading.
supported_as_explicit_editorial_interpretation
One Art uses the villanelle form
Glossary line 40 names the poem in discussion of variant refrains.
relations: The Academy explicitly identifies One Art as a villanelle, so the work-to-form relationship is source_asserted without borrowing the auditor’s interpretation.

identity: Iron-salt photographic process, distinct from photography generally and from photogram as a direct-object arrangement that can use different chemistries.
qualifications: Can record objects permits negatives and other applications; no claim that every cyanotype is a botanical photogram.
claims: Light-sensitive iron salts and water washing create a blue image
Cyanotype process paragraph 155 gives coating, exposure and washing; identification paragraph 152 gives characteristic blue.
Contact placement records specimen shape
Met 10–12 documents Atkins’s directly arranged algae; V&A 155 also describes contact subjects.
relations: Met explicitly identifies Photographs of British Algae as cyanotypes and details the contact-specimen method; exact process-to-work relationship is supported.

identity: Registered Hinduism broad-field control, retaining diversity instead of making puja synonymous with the whole tradition.
qualifications: Diverse, can and particular practice avoid treating every Hindu community as following a single routine. Deity encounter is described as worship practice.
claims: Hindu traditions vary in deities, texts, regional forms and reinterpretation
r18’s thematic prose covers these differences, and r01 explicitly warns to retain internal diversity and change.
Puja can involve images, offerings and visual encounter
Opening 56 and paragraph 67 describe darshan, offerings and contextual variation.
relations: Puja is a documented entry point into the wider traditions; its selection as a learning bridge is properly labeled editorial.

identity: Existing Judaism broad-field control, allowing religious, textual, historical and communal dimensions rather than reducing identity to belief alone.
qualifications: The card offers scriptural interpretation as one way, not the sole definition of Jewish life. It does not imply all Jews share the same religious commitments.
claims: Jewish life interrelates sacred texts, practice, culture, peoplehood and history
Introduction summaries and the linked full essay support this broad framing.
Talmud preserves disputation and commentary as part of teaching
r11 definition explicitly includes rabbinic disputation; r20 line 169 names rabbinic dialogues.
relations: The editorial use of Talmud as an example is supported by its recorded relation to Rabbinic Judaism and dialogic textual form.

identity: Non-participating narrator status, distinct from focalization/information limits and from narrative level. Opposite participation status of homodiegetic is preserved.
qualifications: Without participating concerns the narrated events, not absence of an act of telling; the card correctly avoids equating heterodiegetic with omniscient or simply third person.
claims: Heterodiegetic narrators do not participate in their narrated story
Status 91–94 combines participation with level and maps heterodiegetic to non-diegetic.
Narrative information and level need separate examination
l01 makes level a separate axis; l08 39–50 defines selected/restricted information.
relations: The source explicitly contrasts homo- and heterodiegetic narrators by participation and separates both from traditional grammatical-person shorthand.

identity: Existing Islam broad-field control, with salat as a situated example rather than the identity of Islam as a whole.
qualifications: Differences in interpretation/practice are retained; the card does not universalize every detailed prayer custom from the source.
claims: Commitments to God, Muhammad and Qur’an coexist with diversity
Introduction 149–169 states foundations and differing interpretation/leadership.
Prayer connects preparation, direction and repeated bodily actions
Summary 149 and detailed sequence 156–160 explicitly establish these elements.
relations: Qibla is explicitly the Mecca-oriented direction of Muslim prayer. The broad-field-to-specific-practice bridge is clearly labeled editorial.

identity: The named author, distinct from her separately selected novel. The card provides a documented creative method rather than a bare biographical label.
qualifications: Explicitly distinguishes literary transformation from autobiography; cultural value claims are attributed to Hurston’s commitment.
claims: Hurston brought Black folklore and everyday idiom into fiction
Introduction 36 and author account 47 directly link cultural preservation with literary practice.
A survived hurricane became material in a non-autobiographical novel
Paragraph 35 explicitly describes the incident and the fiction/autobiography distinction.
relations: NEA directly connects Hurston’s life and cultural commitments with Their Eyes Were Watching God, supporting the particular author-to-work link.

identity: Named English-ghazal anthology, distinct from its editor and from the generic ghazal form.
qualifications: Differing fidelity preserves variation among contributions; the invitation to compare maintained/loosened features is a learning prompt, not a claim all poems vary in exactly the same way.
claims: Ali assembled an anthology of English ghazals with differing formal fidelity
Paragraph 44 explicitly identifies the anthology, editorship and variation.
Autonomous couplets and recurring rhyme/refrain offer comparison dimensions
Form definition 27–28 and example 45 support these named structural features.
relations: Paragraph 44 explicitly credits Ali with assembling the book, so the anthology/editor relationship is directly supported.

identity: Specific Azerbaijani village-route-pasture World Heritage landscape, distinct from a village alone or transhumance as a general practice.
qualifications: Connected landscape interpretation stays within UNESCO’s delineation; card avoids unsupported claims that the mobile system is invulnerable or universally sustainable.
claims: The property includes mountain village, seasonal pasture areas and a connecting route
Brief synthesis 38–40 explicitly lists these components.
Summer and winter places form one living seasonal system
The same passage and criteria 41–43 explain vertical transhumance and its living cultural economy.
relations: UNESCO expressly names seasonal transhumance as the practice connecting the listed components, establishing the actual place/practice relationship.

identity: Rashi the named commentator, not Rashbam or peshat as a general method. The cached lesson separates Rashbam’s example from a later Rashi section.
qualifications: Often and his stated approach preserve the source’s bounded methodological claim. Current-page verification is unavailable; substantive assessment is based on the actual cached source passage.
claims: Rashi proceeds line by line and identifies questions in wording
Cached Rashi section 110–111 explicitly states this method.
He joins contextual peshat with selected explanatory aggadah
Cached Rashi on Genesis 3:8:1 at 113–117 and analysis 118–122 explicitly connect the two.
relations: The actual cached text explicitly names Rashi and peshat in the same methodological discussion and quotation; this supports related_to the pinned contextual-reading target. Fresh live access was not obtained.

identity: Named artist’s documented account of practice, distinct from monotype generally and from the separate Peyton work identity.
qualifications: Comparison is attributed to Peyton. The workable-pigment window does not claim no artistic decision occurs after printing in other mixed-media practices.
claims: Peyton contrasts dense painting revisions with quick monotype work
The quoted comparison in 27–28 directly supplies her account.
A monotype plate can be revised before pigment dries and printing fixes marks
Time discussion 26–28 explicitly supplies the process constraint.
relations: The museum directly discusses monotype’s place in Peyton’s practice and her own comparison, supporting the exact artist-to-process relation.

identity: Thoreau’s named literary account, not Walden Pond as a place or a generic withdrawal practice.
qualifications: The documented residence and influence are supported. The final sentence’s explanation of enduring influence is an unmarked editorial causal inference and should be qualified.
claims: Walden recounts time by the pond and inspired dissent from conventional society
Literary Allusions 41–42 expressly states the cabin account and later influence.
Its continuing influence is partly caused by translating the experiment into reusable questions
The brief NEA note documents influence but does not explain this causal mechanism. It is defensible only as an expressly editorial reading/reader invitation.
unmarked_editorial_inference
relations: NEA explicitly calls Walden a precursor of Granger’s philosophy in Fahrenheit 451. The work-to-work relationship is source-asserted and unaffected by the card’s causal overclaim.

findings.finding: The card turns documented influence into an asserted explanation of why it continues. The cited passage does not establish that explanatory cause.

correction: Replace the final sentence with an explicitly editorial reading or invitation to readers to reconsider ways of living. Preserve documented residence, influence and the supported Fahrenheit 451 relation.

identity: Ashbery’s named sestina, distinct from the general form and from Pound’s different example.
qualifications: The comic/melancholic reading is directly documented critical commentary from the Academy, rather than an unstated inference from only the poem’s title or cast.
claims: Popeye characters occur inside a sestina
Example paragraph 63 explicitly identifies cast, author, title and form.
End-word recurrence creates comic surprise with domestic pathos and playful resistance
The same critical paragraph explicitly describes each of these effects.
relations: The glossary expressly calls this work an instance of sestina and contrasts it with Pound’s; the relation to resolved Q1334127 is directly supported.

identity: Named Acadian cultural landscape, distinct from its coastal strip-allotment facet and the broader cultural-landscape field.
qualifications: Does not erase the displacement history: historical memory language summarizes documented deportation commemoration without claiming uninterrupted Acadian ownership.
claims: Working marshland/dykes coexist with archaeology and monuments
Brief synthesis 34–38 names these material elements.
Agricultural continuity and later commemoration jointly carry historical memory
Paragraphs 35–40 explicitly describe maintained farming and memorial significance.
relations: UNESCO specifically identifies preserved coastal strip land divisions within the larger agricultural landscape, supporting the whole-site-to-facet connection.

identity: Existing Q252485 named-design control. The cited Met impression illustrates Hokusai’s design; no new identity is incorrectly minted for that impression.
qualifications: The discovery card’s perspective/scale account is supported. The takeaway assigns a scale-binding purpose to blue pigments that the source does not state.
claims: Perspective/framing make Mount Fuji small within the towering wave
Curatorial line 10 explicitly describes Fuji’s triangular appearance in the crest.
Blue pigments bind the scale contrast
The source separately mentions Hokusai’s palette but not this compositional-purpose claim. Remove the causal purpose or mark it editorial.
unmarked_editorial_inference
relations: The museum explicitly classifies the exact work as a woodblock print, supporting related_to the pinned Printmaking field. That link does not depend on the unsupported color-purpose phrase.

findings.finding: The source supports perspective and a blue palette separately; it does not state blue pigments were used to bind the contrast of scale.

correction: Keep the supported perspective/scale takeaway, or explicitly label the proposed color-function reading editorial. No change to Q252485 or its Printmaking relation is required.
